about:
Every whisker as ONE continuous line, from its root on his whisker pad to its tip. Owner, 2026-11-14: "whiskers don't just abruptly cut off - that's not how they work ...
it is in our best interest to trace the little guy's whiskers to them [the pads] now, so we
don't go hunting for whisker connections on his little round body in a few steps." And the
rule: whiskers come out of his whisker pads, point toward them, and are straight.

pads.about: the whole raised muzzle around his nose and mouth (owner, 2026-11-14), measured as the closed shading crease where it turns away; split at the philtrum into his two pads; judgment boundary, owner review

whiskers.why: one arc through the outside and face parts fits to 0.45 px (gap 22 px)
one arc fits to 1.6 px; points at his pad. (FW-13 fits B2-S02 better, 0.7 px, but does not point at a pad)

your L05. Starts on B2-S02's outside root stretch (one arc 0.7 px), so it shares that stretch. FLAG: 2-4x darker than any whisker on his face, runs along the inside edge of his fur band, and points 158 px off the pad (toward his eye); to reach the pad it must bend more than any whisker
whiskers.doubt: to reach the pad outline it must bend -0.14 deg/px against its own +0.11 (whiskers on his face bend at most 0.25); it points away from its pad: it may not be a pad whisker

whiskers.why: one arc fits to 0.10 px (gap 8 px)
one arc fits to 0.32 px (gap 6 px)
FW-03 + B2-S20: one arc 0.73 px; B2-S20 + B2-S29 (the 'loose' piece): one arc 0.28 px across a 45 px stretch where the light whisker doesn't show against the white background
no face line on its arc (best: B2-S16-face, 4.9 px off): its face part is under the fur
no face line of its own (B2-S16-face is 12 px off, one arc 2.0 px; B2-S16 owns it at 0.32 px): its face part is under the fur
your L10. W-F01 (traced as a fine light hair) fits it: one arc 0.54 px, gap 32 px. (B2-S03, 8 px beside W-F01, is a separate hair)
your L11. Reaches his outline beside B2-S08's root; B2-S08 is not its outside part (one arc 4.3 px; B2-S08's root stretch carries one whisker's darkness, 1.04x): goes round his cheek
whiskers.outer_end: out of view: reaches his outline with nothing outside, so it goes round his cheek

whiskers.why: your L04 + L17; nothing outside on its line
whiskers.outer_end: goes under the fur 40 px inside his outline (stops at 1.8x its usual darkness, not tapering); where its line meets his outline nothing comes out

whiskers.why: your L07 + L18; nothing outside on its line
whiskers.outer_end: goes under the fur 43 px inside his outline (stops at 1.3x its usual darkness, not tapering); where its line meets his outline nothing comes out

whiskers.why: your L06; by his mouth, far from his outline
whiskers.outer_end: fades like a tip, 230 px inside his outline (last 20 px at 0.5x its usual darkness)

whiskers.why: one arc fits to 0.28 px (gap 10 px)
traced as a borderline wisp (34 px, straight). Fits B4-S02-face too (one arc 0.78 px, 2 deg), and B4-S02-face is the darkest line on that cheek (1.5-2x its neighbours): two whiskers share it
one arc fits to 0.42 px (gap 8 px)
starts exactly on B5-S17's root (one arc 1.2 px); B5-S17's root stretch is 2.8x as dark as the rest of it (B2-S08 and B1-S11, also rooted at the outline: 1.0x): two whiskers share that stretch
the fan (three whiskers on one root line). FW-05 fits all three (0.37-0.55 px) but carries one whisker's darkness; B4-S17 fits best (0.37 px, smallest bend)
the fan: shares B4-S17's root line outside, so it bends into the cheek the same way; its face part is under the fur alongside FW-05 (FW-05 carries one whisker's darkness)
